Methods for Sequential Check Objects

Source: R/smsd_check.R
smsd_check_methods.Rd

Methods for the smsd_check objects returned by the sequential check functions (the seq_aipe_* accuracy in parameter estimation family, the seq_mr_* and seq_br_* minimum risk and bounded risk families, the fixed width and two stage procedures, and the budget constrained method).

Usage

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
format(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
print(x, digits = getOption("digits"), ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
summary(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
as.data.frame(x, row.names = NULL, optional = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
tidy(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'smsd_check'
glance(x, ...)

Arguments

x, object

An object of class "smsd_check".

digits

Number of significant digits to show for numeric values; by default the session's getOption("digits"). Stored values are never rounded; this affects display only.

...

Not used.

row.names, optional

Ignored; present for compatibility with the generic.

Value

print() returns its input invisibly. format() returns a character vector, one element per printed line. summary() and glance() return a one row data.frame with columns method, estimate_term, estimate, lower_limit, upper_limit, current_n, criterion_n, is_satisfied, conf_level, and width (NA where the procedure has no such quantity). tidy() returns a one row data.frame with columns term, estimate, ci_lower, ci_upper, and conf_level. as.data.frame() returns a data.frame with columns term and value.

Details

print() shows the method, the current and criterion sample sizes, the target width and confidence level when the procedure has them, every term, whether the stopping rule is met, and any notes (for example that the variance estimate is not yet usable, in which case the rule is reported as not met). For a check from seq_budget at which sampling has ended because the budget cannot pay for another needed observation, with a group still below its criterion, the stopping line reads FALSE (sampling has ended: the budget is exhausted), because the rule itself was not met; the attribute is_satisfied, which says whether sampling has ended, is TRUE. format() returns the same lines as a character vector. summary() and glance() return a one row data frame describing the check; tidy() returns the point estimate with its confidence limits in the column layout used by the sibling package DMAR. as.data.frame() returns the plain term/value data frame without the class or the sequential attributes. Subsetting with [ returns a plain data frame (or vector) whenever the result is no longer the complete check, so a partial object is never printed as if it were a complete one.

Width and coverage. An AIPE check carries attr(x, "coverage_guarantee") = "asymptotic". Its display and seq_report distinguish the asymptotic confidence level from satisfying the width criterion. The latter does not establish nominal coverage at the observed sample size. See vignette("coverage-and-design", package = "SMSD") for measured operating characteristics and simulation uncertainty.

A check that cannot be evaluated. In a small sample the estimate of the variance that a stopping rule needs can be zero, negative, or not finite. No variance has then been estimated: the stopping flag is FALSE, attr(x, "variance_unusable") is TRUE, and a note says so. This is a deliberate departure from the stopping rules as printed in the source articles, under which such an estimate, or the lower bound \(n^{-3}\) that some of them put in its place, would make the rule be met at once. A positive estimate, however small, is used as the articles prescribe (with that bound where an article has one). When the point estimate itself is not finite, the flag is FALSE as well and a note gives the reason. (The two stage ts_* functions whose total sample size the first stage variance or scale fixes stop with an error on a first stage with no variation instead; see SMSD.) Test attr(x, "is_satisfied"), which is always TRUE or FALSE, to drive a sampling loop. What the limit rows then hold depends on the procedure. The seq_aipe_* functions report NA for both limits. The seq_fwd_* functions still report their limits, which are computed from the estimate and d alone and involve no variance. seq_budget still reports an interval, computed with a variance of zero for each group whose variance is unusable, which is too narrow. Neither of the last two is an interval to report. summary(), glance(), and tidy() return the limits as stored, without the notes or variance_unusable, so test attr(x, "variance_unusable") before using them.

An object that is no longer one check. Some operations leave the class on something that is not a check as the function returned it: rbind() of two or more checks (which keeps the attributes of the first), a data frame verb of another package that binds checks, or an attribute removed by hand. print(), format(), summary(), tidy(), glance(), and seq_report stop with a message that says so, rather than describe the object as if it were one complete check. as.data.frame() always works and gives the plain table. To keep a record of the stages of a study, bind the one row summary() of each check, or use seq_path, which records every stage.

Author

Ken Kelley kkelley@nd.edu

Examples

set.seed(113)
group_1 <- rnorm(40, mean = 0.5)
group_2 <- rnorm(40, mean = 0)
out <- seq_aipe_smd(group_1, group_2, width = 0.50)
out
#> Sequential check (standardized mean difference)
#> 
#>   Current n       : 40
#>   Criterion n     : 125
#>   Target width    : 0.5
#>   Confidence level: 95%
#>   Coverage        : asymptotic; assess with sensitivity analysis
#> 
#>   lower_limit       : 0.08665111
#>   smd               : 0.5257976
#>   upper_limit       : 0.964944
#>   xi_squared        : 2.008087
#>   criterion_n       : 125
#>   current_n         : 40
#> 
#>   Stopping rule met: FALSE
summary(out)
#>                         method estimate_term  estimate lower_limit upper_limit
#> 1 standardized mean difference           smd 0.5257976  0.08665111    0.964944
#>   current_n criterion_n is_satisfied conf_level width
#> 1        40         125        FALSE       0.95   0.5
generics::tidy(out)
#>   term  estimate   ci_lower ci_upper conf_level
#> 1  smd 0.5257976 0.08665111 0.964944       0.95
as.data.frame(out)
#>          term        value
#> 1 lower_limit   0.08665111
#> 2         smd   0.52579756
#> 3 upper_limit   0.96494402
#> 4  xi_squared   2.00808721
#> 5 criterion_n 125.00000000
#> 6   current_n  40.00000000
out[out$term == "smd", "value"]
#> [1] 0.5257976
